name: How long does an ADU kitchen build take after permits are approved?

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to build the kitchen portion of an ADU once construction starts?
mainEntity.text: How long does it take to build the kitchen portion of an ADU once construction starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once permits are approved and construction begins, the kitchen itself is usually one of the final major phases of an ADU build. The rough plumbing, electrical, framing adjustments, insulation, drywall, and inspections have to happen before cabinets, counters, tile, and appliances can go in. A simple kitchen can move quickly if materials are ordered early and the layout is straightforward. A custom kitchen may take longer because cabinets, countertops, and specialty appliances often have lead times and require precise coordination. Delays usually come from late design changes, backordered fixtures, or countertop templating problems rather than the actual installation work. For Los Angeles-area projects, it is smart to ask the contractor for a kitchen-specific schedule, not just a general ADU timeline. That schedule should show when rough-ins finish, when cabinets arrive, when counters are measured, and when final appliance hookups are expected. This keeps the kitchen from becoming the bottleneck at the end of the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: The kitchen portion of an ADU build often takes several weeks after rough utilities and inspections are complete. Timing depends on cabinet lead times, countertop fabrication, appliance delivery, and how much plumbing or electrical work is needed. Complex custom kitchens take longer than simple compact layouts.
